# 1 Enoch Chapter 74 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 1 Enoch Chapter 74 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 74:10-16 — Handling the arithmetic passages

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | Full Ge'ez construct chains with hyphens | Maximum fidelity to source structure |
| LOGOS | Clean prose with spelled-out numbers | Readable while maintaining precision |
| PNEUMA | Modern numerals (1,092 etc.) | Maximum clarity for modern readers |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS prose with spelled-out numbers. The use of modern numerals (PNEUMA) is anachronistic for a translation of an ancient text; the spelled-out numbers better reflect the rhetorical weight of the enumeration in the original. Hyphenated construct chains (EMET) are unnecessarily difficult for this mathematical content.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Clarity without anachronism.

---

## 74:12 — 'exact justice' for the 364-day year

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "with exact-justice" | Literal; the Ge'ez term implies both precision and rectitude |
| LOGOS | "with exact justice" | Same, clean prose |
| PNEUMA | "with perfect accuracy" | Modern equivalent of the concept |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted 'exact justice' (EMET/LOGOS). This phrase carries theological weight — the 364-day year is not merely accurate but righteous, fulfilling the divine order. 'Exact justice' captures both the mathematical precision and the moral/theological dimension that 'accuracy' alone loses.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS. Theological resonance preserved.

---

## 74:11 — 'falls behind' vs. 'lags' vs. 'deficit'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "falls-behind" | Traditional; preserves the directional metaphor |
| LOGOS | "falls behind" | Clean prose |
| PNEUMA | "falls behind" | All three agree |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** All three converge on 'falls behind.' No dispute.

**Status:** Converged.

---
